Bringen or Holen? German A2 Movement Verb Practice

Distinguish bringing something to a destination from going to fetch it. Practise bringen and holen with explicit movement cues.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Bringen focuses on carrying or taking something to a destination: Ich bringe dir den Ordner. Holen focuses on going to get something or someone: Ich hole den Ordner aus dem Büro. In a real sequence, someone can fetch an item first and bring it afterwards.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not assume that the verbs describe unrelated actions. The same delivery can involve holen at the collection point and bringen at the destination.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich bringe dir den Ordner an deinen Schreibtisch.I bring the folder to your desk.
Worked example 2Sie holt ihre Tochter von der Musikschule.She fetches her daughter from music school.
Worked example 3Wir bringen dem Nachbarn seine Post.We bring the neighbour his post.
Worked example 4Kannst du Wasser aus dem Keller holen?Can you fetch water from the cellar?

Practice: choose the right word

Use bringen for delivery to the stated recipient and holen for fetching from the stated collection point. Conjugate in the present. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich ___ den Koffer aus dem Auto. (go and fetch)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: hole

Holen highlights going to the car to get the suitcase.

Question 2. Der Kellner ___ uns die Speisekarte an den Tisch. (delivery)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: bringt

Bringen highlights delivery to the diners.

Question 3. Wir müssen die Tickets am Schalter ___. (collect)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: holen

Collecting something from a collection point uses holen.

Question 4. ___ du mir morgen die Unterlagen mit? (bring along)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: Bringst

The full verb is mitbringen; its finite du form is bringst with mit at the end.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
